editor.jobOutputContractHint: Scripts return a fixed envelope; put business fields in each host's results[].data and emit BK_LITE_RESULT=. Follow this when a downstream Document Render node builds a report, or when other nodes consume structured results.
editor.reportFixedContractBody: The structured output envelope of a job-execute node is fixed by the platform: summary, results, target, status, exit_code, and error. Do not rename these fields in scripts.
editor.reportCustomDataBody: Put business content in each host's results[].data. Objects, arrays, and nested structures are allowed up to 10 levels deep.
editor.reportScriptMarkerBody: Write one BK_LITE_RESULT=<JSON object> line to stdout. The platform parses that marker from the full stdout; without it, data is an empty object.
editor.reportDataToTemplateBody: The document-render node renders in-process: Word via docxtpl and Excel via xlsxjinja. The template root is that JSON with no extra d wrapper: summary is the rollup, results is the host array, and results[n].data holds each host's script payload.
editor.reportDataToTemplateHost: One results item is created per host; looped table rows follow the array length.
editor.reportDataToTemplateMetric: Per-host arrays such as metrics or critical can be expanded with nested loops.
editor.reportHowItWorksBody: Design the final report layout in Word or Excel and place Jinja placeholders where values should appear. Word and Excel share Jinja style but use different loop tags—follow the two sections below. Fonts, colors, and layout stay as you designed them in Office.
editor.reportWordNoteLayout: Titles, explanatory paragraphs, and multiple independent tables are all fine. A summary table plus severity-specific detail tables is the recommended pattern.
editor.reportWordNoteStaticMerge: Static merged cells outside loops, such as title spans or header notes, are supported and preserved.
editor.reportWordNoteNestedTable: Tables nested inside cells can work, but separate side-by-side tables are safer than deep nested tables.
editor.reportWordNoteEmptyChapter: An empty array produces no looped data rows, but static chapter titles remain. Hiding whole chapters when empty is not a verified product capability yet; validate any conditional syntax with a sample template first.
editor.reportExcelNotePerSheet: Every worksheet that loops needs its own matching {% for %} / {% endfor %} pair.
editor.reportExcelNoteMerge: Keep static merged title cells outside the loop range. Loop markers must not cross or split existing merges.
editor.reportExcelNoteVertical: Prefer vertical row repetition. Do not rely on runtime dynamic merges or dynamic charts.
editor.reportExcelNoteStaticOk: Pre-merged header or cover cells are fine as long as they stay outside the loop range.
editor.reportSupportedReplace: Single-value replacement for summary fields, host name, IP, and script data fields
editor.reportSupportedLoop: Vertical loop expansion for arrays, including one nested loop level
editor.reportSupportedStaticMerge: Static merged cells and normal Word/Excel styling outside loops
editor.reportSupportedMultiTable: Multiple independent tables in one document, and separate loops per worksheet
editor.reportUnsupportedDynamicMerge: Dynamic cell merges driven by loop data
editor.reportUnsupportedLoopAcrossMerge: Loop markers that cross existing merged regions
editor.reportUnsupportedCharts: Dynamic charts and arbitrary two-dimensional expansion
editor.reportExampleFilesBody: Download the Word and Excel samples from the parameter area. Start from those placeholders, then adapt titles, columns, and field paths.

editor.reportWordSyntaxBody: Use {{ }} for fields. Loops that span paragraphs or table rows must use {%p ... %} / {%tr ... %}; plain {% for %} cannot cross paragraphs or rows.
editor.reportWordLoopHint: Put the start and end tags on their own rows. Fill the middle row with {{ r.field }}; the engine copies that row once per array item.
editor.reportExcelSyntaxBody: Fields also use {{ }}. Loops use plain {% for %} / {% endfor %} in cells; each worksheet that needs looping must define its own pair.
